lessons.title: Die Zimmer: Das Bad ist klein
lessons.goal: Name the rooms of a home and describe each with sein + adjective (nicht / ziemlich / sehr / zu).

grammar.point: After sein an adjective never changes. Add a degree word before it: nicht < ziemlich < sehr; zu = too much (a problem).
grammar.oneLine: Das Badezimmer ist ziemlich klein. Der Keller ist zu klein.

mistake.why: After ist the adjective never gets an ending: it stays groß, whatever the article is.

terms.meaning: a word that says how something is: groß, klein, schön
letters added to the end of a word; after ist an adjective gets none
a small word before the adjective: nicht, ziemlich, sehr, zu
more than one: das Bad, die Bäder

cards.title: Before we start: show someone your home
cards.body: Chapter 9 is about your home: rooms, a flat ad, furniture and where things are. Today you name the rooms and say how they are. You know Das Zimmer ist groß. Now you add room names and small words like ziemlich.

examples.en: The room is big.
examples.why: You know this: sein + an adjective (chapter 3).

examples.en: The bathroom is quite small.
examples.why: New today: a room name and ziemlich.

steps: You already know: sein + an adjective, e.g. Das Zimmer ist groß, and sehr / zu / nicht (chapter 3); Wohnung, Haus, Zimmer (chapter 5)
New today: nine room words, ziemlich, and the ladder nicht, ziemlich, sehr, zu
By the end you can: name the rooms of a home, say how each room is, and say on which floor it is
cards.more: Imagine you show a friend your flat on a video call. You walk from room to room and say what each room is and how it is: big, small, quiet. You already have the sentence for it: the room, then ist, then an adjective. Today you only add new room names and a few small words that you put in front of the adjective, like a volume knob. Nothing else about the sentence changes, and you can say a lot with it.

cards.title: The rooms of a home
cards.body: Most room words end in -zimmer, so they are das-words. Learn each word with its article. Bad is the short, everyday word for Badezimmer. Its plural is Bäder, with an Umlaut.

examples.en: The house has a cellar.
examples.why: der Keller: you know einen after hat.

examples.en: The flat has a balcony.
Mira has a bedroom.

cards.more: Think of a home as a big box with smaller boxes inside. Each small box has a name. The names ending in -zimmer all belong to the das family, so you only learn one rule for all of them. Bad is just a short nickname for Badezimmer. People say Bad every day because it is quicker. The other room words, like Balkon, Garten and Keller, are der-words, and Dusche is a die-word. Say each one out loud with its article.
cards.lead: In the introduction you used one room name. This card gives you all the rooms at once, with their articles and plurals, so you can name every part of a home.

deeper.text: Many room words are two words glued together: Kinder (children) + Zimmer (room) = Kinderzimmer, Schlaf (sleep) + Zimmer = Schlafzimmer. The last word decides the article, so every -zimmer word is das. In real life people often drop the -zimmer: they say Wohnzimmer, but just Bad for the bathroom and Küche for the kitchen.

example.en: The children's room is small.

cards.title: Wie ist das Zimmer? sein + adjective
cards.body: To describe a room, use ist and an adjective. After ist the adjective never changes: no ending, ever. Das Wohnzimmer ist groß, never großes.

examples.en: The living room is big.
The garden is nice.
examples.why: der Garten, but schön stays schön.

examples.en: The shower is new.
examples.why: die Dusche, and neu has no ending.

steps: Name the room: das Wohnzimmer
Add ist: Das Wohnzimmer ist
Add the adjective, no ending: Das Wohnzimmer ist groß.
cards.more: A German adjective after ist is like a label on a box. The label always says the same thing, no matter if the box is a der-box, a die-box or a das-box. Der Garten ist schön. Die Dusche ist schön. Das Zimmer ist schön. The word schön never gets a new ending here. You know many adjectives already: groß, klein, schön, laut, ruhig, teuer, neu, alt. Now you can use them with every room.
cards.lead: The first card gave you the room names. Here you describe them: one short pattern with ist and an adjective, which works for every room and every adjective you know.

deeper.text: The adjective after ist has no ending, whatever the article is. English does the same: the room is big, the garden is big. You can also put two adjectives after ist with und: Das Zimmer ist klein und ruhig. Both stay bare. Only an adjective before a noun gets an ending, and you meet that later.

example.de: Das Schlafzimmer ist klein und ruhig.
example.en: The bedroom is small and quiet.

cards.title: The ladder: nicht, ziemlich, sehr, zu
cards.body: A small word before the adjective says how much. It goes up like a ladder: nicht groß, ziemlich groß (quite big), sehr groß (very big). zu groß is different: too big, which is a problem.

examples.en: The bathroom is not big.
The child's room is quite small.
The cellar is too small.
examples.why: zu = too, more than you want.

steps: nicht groß: not big
ziemlich groß: quite big
sehr groß: very big
zu groß: too big (a problem)
cards.more: Picture a volume knob with four marks. At nicht the room does not have that quality. At ziemlich the knob is in the middle, at sehr it is high. Zu is past the last mark: too much, and that is a problem. Step 1: say the room and ist. Step 2: pick the mark: nicht, ziemlich, sehr or zu. Step 3: say the adjective with no ending. Extra example: Der Garten ist sehr schön. = The garden is very nice.
cards.lead: You can now say a room is big or small. This card adds four small words that put the adjective on a scale, so you can say how big and whether that is good or bad.

deeper.text: One small word changes the mood. Das Zimmer ist klein only describes the room. Das Zimmer ist zu klein is a complaint: it is smaller than you want. Sehr is strong too, but it is only strong, not a problem. So sehr klein is a fact, and zu klein is something you may want to change.

example.en: The room is too small.

cards.title: nicht or sehr? One room or many rooms
cards.body: For one room use ist. For more than one room use sind. The adjective still has no ending. Compare nicht schön and sehr schön: one small word changes the whole message.

examples.en: The room is not nice.
The room is very nice.
The rooms are very nice.
examples.why: Many rooms: sind, and schön still has no ending.

cards.more: Count the rooms first. One room needs ist, two or more need sind, and the adjective stays bare in both cases. Step 1: count the rooms. Step 2: choose ist or sind. Step 3: add the ladder word and the adjective, with no ending. Step 4: check the meaning: nicht schön and sehr schön say opposite things. Extra example: Die Zimmer sind ziemlich ruhig. = The rooms are quite quiet.
cards.lead: Now you can say how a room is. This card adds the plural: with more than one room the verb becomes sind, and the ladder words work exactly as before.

deeper.text: When you describe two things with the same adjective, join them with und and use sind: Das Bad und die Küche sind klein. Two things together always count as many, even if each one is singular. English works the same way: the bathroom and the kitchen are small, never is small.

example.de: Das Bad und die Küche sind klein.
example.en: The bathroom and the kitchen are small.

cards.title: Rooms and floors: im Erdgeschoss
cards.body: Where is the room? Learn these four chunks whole for now: im Erdgeschoss (on the ground floor), in der ersten Etage (on the first floor), im Wohnzimmer, im Garten. Lesson 3 explains the rule behind them.

examples.en: The kitchen is on the ground floor.

examples.de: Das Schlafzimmer ist in der ersten Etage.
examples.en: The bedroom is on the first floor.
examples.why: in der ersten Etage = one piece.

examples.en: Mira is in the garden.

rows: im Erdgeschoss, in der ersten Etage

cards.more: You already know im Büro and in der Kantine from chapter 7. Today you only copy the same pattern with new places. Think of im Erdgeschoss and in der ersten Etage as little blocks that you put at the end of the sentence, like stickers. You do not have to take them apart now. In lesson 3 you open the blocks and see why it is im and in der.
cards.lead: You can describe rooms. This card tells where they are: four ready-made chunks for floors and places that you can put at the end of a sentence, without any new rules.

deeper.text: Careful with floors. The German Erdgeschoss is the floor at street level, and die erste Etage is the next one up, like British English. In American English that would be the second floor. Many Germans also say der erste Stock for the same floor: im ersten Stock means the same as in der ersten Etage.

example.de: Das Bad ist im ersten Stock.
example.en: The bathroom is on the first floor.

cards.title: Questions: Wie ist ...? Ist ... groß?
cards.body: Ask Wie ist das Zimmer? and answer with an adjective. A yes/no question starts with ist: Ist das Bad groß? Say Ja, es ist groß. or Nein, es ist nicht groß.

examples.en: How is the room?
Is the bathroom big?
examples.why: Yes/no question: the verb comes first.

examples.en: No, it is not big.

cards.more: There are two kinds of questions. With a question word, like wie, the question word comes first and the verb is second: Wie ist das Zimmer? Without a question word, the verb jumps to the very front: Ist das Bad groß? You can answer with Ja or Nein and then a full sentence. Use es for das-words, er for der-words and sie for die-words, so you do not repeat the noun.
cards.lead: Now you can describe rooms. This last card lets you ask about them, with Wie ist ...? and with yes/no questions, and answer in a short, natural way.

deeper.text: To avoid saying the same noun again, use er for der-words, sie for die-words and es for das-words, even for things: Ist der Garten schön? Ja, er ist sehr schön. Here er means it, not he. In a short answer, Ja or Nein stands first, then a comma, then the full sentence.

example.en: Yes, it is very nice.

lessons.title: Die Wohnungsanzeige: Größe, Miete, Lage
lessons.goal: Read a short flat ad (rooms, size, rent, place) and say what the flat has and has not.

grammar.point: nicht negates an adjective or a verb (Die Wohnung ist nicht groß); kein / keine / keinen negates a noun (Sie hat keinen Balkon).
grammar.oneLine: Die Wohnung ist nicht groß. Die Wohnung hat keinen Balkon.

mistake.why: Balkon is a noun, so you say no with kein-: der Balkon becomes keinen Balkon. nicht is for adjectives and verbs.

terms.meaning: saying no to something: nicht or kein
a short form of a word, e.g. Zi. for Zimmer
rent without heating and other costs
the person who rents the flat to you: der Vermieter, die Vermieterin

cards.title: Before we start: read a flat ad
cards.body: Today you read a short flat ad and say what the flat has and has not. You know Ich habe keinen Laptop from chapter 4. Now the same keinen describes a flat: Die Wohnung hat keinen Balkon.

examples.en: I do not have a laptop.
examples.why: You know this: keinen + a der-word.

examples.en: The flat has no balcony.
examples.why: New today: the same keinen, now for a flat.

steps: You already know: kein / keinen for nouns and nicht for adjectives (chapter 4); rooms and sein + adjective (lesson 1); numbers (chapters 2 and 4)
New today: how a flat ad is built, hell / dunkel / modern / frei, suchen and mieten, and when to use nicht and when kein
By the end you can: read a short flat ad, say what the flat has and has not, and say that you look for a flat
cards.more: When you look for a flat, you read many short ads. They are full of tiny words and signs, because every letter costs money. Today you learn to decode them, like a secret code. Then you can say what the flat has and what it does not have. You already know the two small tools for that: nicht and kein. The new part is to choose the right one, and to read numbers like 75 and 850 aloud.

cards.title: The anatomy of a short ad
cards.body: Flat ads are very short. They use abbreviations: Zi. = Zimmer, m² = Quadratmeter, KM = Kaltmiete (rent without extras), ab = from. Read the ad piece by piece: rooms, size, rent, extras, date, place.

examples.en: The flat has three rooms.
The flat is 75 square metres.

examples.de: Die Wohnung ist ab 1. Mai frei.
examples.en: The flat is free from 1 May.
examples.why: ab 1. Mai frei = available from 1 May.

steps: Rooms: 3 Zi.
Size: 75 m²
Rent: 850 € KM
Extra: Balkon
Date: ab 1. Mai frei
Place: Zentrum
cards.more: An ad is like a text message in code. Instead of Die Wohnung hat drei Zimmer, it says 3 Zi. Instead of fünfundsiebzig Quadratmeter, it says 75 m². You do not need to write the code, only to read it. Go from left to right and ask a small question for each piece: how many rooms, how big, how much, what extras, from when, where? The ad is then a full little description of the flat.
cards.lead: Lesson 1 gave you the rooms. This card shows how an ad packs rooms, size, rent and place into a few signs, so you can decode a real ad from left to right.

deeper.text: In an ad, 3 Zi. counts only the main rooms: living and sleeping rooms. The kitchen, the bathroom and the hall are usually not counted. So a 3-Zimmer flat has, for example, a living room and two bedrooms, plus a kitchen and a bath. A 1-Zimmer flat is one room with a small kitchen: perfect for a student.

example.de: Die Wohnung hat ein Wohnzimmer und zwei Schlafzimmer.
example.en: The flat has a living room and two bedrooms.

cards.title: Numbers in ads: rent and size
cards.body: Rent and size are numbers. You know hundert from chapter 2. 850 is achthundertfünfzig, written as one word. In 75 the ones come first: fünfundsiebzig, which is fünf + und + siebzig.

examples.en: The rent is 850 euros.

examples.de: Die Wohnung ist fünfundsiebzig Quadratmeter groß.
examples.en: The flat is 75 square metres.

examples.de: Das Zimmer ist zwanzig Quadratmeter groß.
examples.en: The room is 20 square metres.

cards.more: Big numbers in German are built like Lego, and they are one long word. Take the hundreds first: drei-hundert. Then the ones, then und, then the tens: fünf-und-siebzig. So 375 is dreihundertfünfundsiebzig. It looks long, but the pieces are small. Read the rent first, then the size. Euro and Quadratmeter do not change after a number, so you say fünfundsiebzig Quadratmeter, never Quadratmeters.
cards.lead: You can decode the signs of an ad. Now the numbers: this card shows how to read rent and size aloud, with hundreds, tens and ones, the way a landlord would say them.

deeper.text: Sizes and prices are not always round. German writes a comma where English writes a point: 75,5 m² is fünfundsiebzig Komma fünf Quadratmeter. With money you say the euros, then the cents, without Komma: 8,50 € is acht Euro fünfzig. Quadratmeter and Euro keep the same form after any number.

example.de: Das Bad ist acht Komma fünf Quadratmeter groß.
example.en: The bathroom is 8.5 square metres.

cards.title: Describing the flat: hell, dunkel, modern, frei
cards.body: Four new adjectives describe a flat: hell (bright, light), dunkel (dark), modern and frei (free, available). Use them with ist, and they have no ending: Die Wohnung ist hell. Im Zentrum means in the centre: learn it as a chunk.

examples.de: Die Wohnung ist hell und modern.
examples.en: The flat is bright and modern.
The bedroom is dark.

examples.de: Die Wohnung ist im Zentrum und ziemlich teuer.
examples.en: The flat is in the centre and quite expensive.

cards.more: You already know how to describe a room: the room, ist, an adjective. Now you have four more adjectives that fit a flat perfectly. Hell is when a lot of light comes in. Dunkel is the opposite. Modern looks like the English word. Frei means that nobody lives there, so you can move in. The little words from lesson 1, like sehr and zu, still work: sehr hell, zu dunkel.
cards.lead: In the ad you saw frei and Zentrum. This card gives you the words to describe the flat in your own sentences, with the same ist + adjective pattern as in lesson 1.

deeper.text: Careful with frei. In an ad it means available: nobody lives there, so you can move in. It does not mean that the flat costs nothing. For no money, Germans say kostenlos. So Die Wohnung ist ab Mai frei is about the date, not the price. Noch frei means still available.

example.en: The room is still available.

cards.title: The flat has: hat + einen / eine / ein
cards.body: An ad lists what the flat has. Use hat and the noun. It is the accusative you know: der → einen, die → eine, das → ein. To say it has none, use keinen, keine, kein.

examples.en: The flat has a balcony.
The flat has a shower.
The flat has no garden.

cards.more: Think of kein as ein with a minus sign. Ein means one. Kein means not one, so none. The endings are the same as for ein: einen, eine, ein become keinen, keine, kein. You know this from chapter 4. After hat the noun is in the accusative, so a der-word gets the -en ending: einen Balkon, keinen Garten. Die-words and das-words do not change: eine Dusche, ein Bad.
cards.lead: You can describe the flat with adjectives. This card says what the flat has and what it has not, with hat and the ein- or kein- word you know from chapter 4.

deeper.text: For a plural noun there is no ein, but there is keine. You can say zwei Balkone (two balconies), but for none you say keine Balkone. A flat in the centre often has keine Gärten, because there is no space for a garden.

example.en: The flats have no gardens.

cards.title: nicht or kein?
cards.body: Two ways to say no. nicht goes with an adjective or a verb: Die Wohnung ist nicht groß. kein goes with a noun: Die Wohnung hat keinen Balkon. Never say ist kein groß.

examples.en: The flat is not expensive.
Ben is not coming.
I do not have a flat.

cards.more: Ask one question: what do I want to say no to? If it is a noun, like Balkon or Wohnung, use kein: it replaces ein. If it is an adjective, like groß or teuer, or the whole action, like kommen, use nicht. So Die Wohnung hat keinen Balkon says no to the balcony. Die Wohnung ist nicht groß says no to big. The two words never swap places, so the wrong versions sound strange in German.
cards.lead: You can say what a flat has and how it is. This card helps you choose between the two ways to say no: nicht for adjectives and verbs, kein for nouns.

deeper.text: One more rule: with der, die, das or mein, you say no with nicht, not kein. Das ist nicht die Wohnung means it is the wrong flat. Das ist keine Wohnung means it is not a flat at all. So kein replaces ein; nicht stands in front of der, die, das or mein.

example.en: That is not my flat.

cards.title: Look for a flat: suchen and mieten
cards.body: To look for something: suchen. Ich suche eine Wohnung. To rent: mieten. Ich möchte eine Wohnung mieten. The landlord is der Vermieter, the landlady die Vermieterin. Add -in for a woman.

examples.en: Mira is looking for a flat.
I would like to rent a flat.
examples.why: möchte + mieten at the end: the bracket you know.

examples.en: The landlady is nice.

cards.more: Two small verbs help you with a flat. Suchen means to look for. Mieten means to rent: you pay money every month, and the flat stays the property of somebody else. The person who owns the flat and rents it to you is the Vermieter. A woman is a Vermieterin. You know the -in trick from Freund and Freundin. Möchte plus a verb at the end is like the bracket with können from chapter 5: Ich möchte eine Wohnung mieten. Extra example: Ben sucht ein Zimmer. = Ben is looking for a room.
cards.lead: You can read an ad and describe a flat. This card lets you say what you do: look for a flat and rent one, and name the person you rent from.

deeper.text: mieten means you pay the owner each month to live in a flat. The owner does the other side: vermieten, to rent out. So der Vermieter vermietet, and der Mieter (the tenant) mietet. Ver- turns the verb around, a bit like English rent and rent out. The opposite of mieten is kaufen, to buy.

example.en: The landlord rents out the flat.

cards.title: Culture: Kaltmiete and pro Monat
cards.body: In Germany most people rent. Ads show the Kaltmiete: the rent without heating and other costs. You pay it pro Monat, per month. The total with heating is higher, so always ask what is included.

examples.de: Die Miete ist achthundertfünfzig Euro pro Monat.
examples.en: The rent is 850 euros a month.
examples.why: pro Monat = per month, one piece.

examples.de: Das Zimmer kostet dreihundert Euro pro Monat.
examples.en: The room costs 300 euros a month.

examples.de: Mira mietet eine Wohnung im Zentrum.
examples.en: Mira rents a flat in the centre.

rows: rent without heating and other costs

cards.more: In Germany it is normal to rent a flat for many years. The price in the ad is usually the Kaltmiete. Kalt means cold, so the price has no heating in it. Heating and water cost extra every month. Together they make the total rent. So when you see 850 € KM, the real price is a bit higher. Pro Monat is a fixed phrase that means each month. You will see it on every contract.
cards.lead: You can read an ad and look for a flat. This short card shows what the rent in an ad really means in Germany, and gives you the useful chunk pro Monat.

deeper.text: KM in an ad stands for Kaltmiete. Often you also see NK for Nebenkosten: heating, water and rubbish. Kaltmiete plus Nebenkosten is the Warmmiete, the real price per month. So 850 € KM + 150 € NK means you pay 1000 euros. Always ask: Wie hoch ist die Warmmiete?

example.de: Die Warmmiete ist tausend Euro pro Monat.
example.en: The total rent is 1000 euros a month.

lessons.title: Möbel: Wo ist das? in, auf, an
lessons.goal: Say where furniture is with in, auf, an + dative (wo?).

grammar.point: Three place words answer Wo? with the dative: in (inside), auf (on top), an (at / against a vertical surface). der / das → dem (im, am), die → der, plural → den + n.
grammar.oneLine: Die Lampe ist auf dem Tisch. Das Bild ist an der Wand.

mistake.wrong: Die Lampe ist auf den Tisch.
mistake.right: Die Lampe ist auf dem Tisch.
mistake.why: Wo? (where something is) needs the dative: der Tisch becomes dem Tisch after auf.

terms.meaning: the case you use after in, auf, an when you say where something is
a small word like in, auf, an that says the place of something
the question word for where something is
two words melted into one: in dem = im, an dem = am

cards.title: Before we start: where is the sofa?
cards.body: Today you say where furniture is. You know Ich arbeite im Büro and Mira ist in der Kantine from chapter 7: in + dative. Now you add two more place words, auf and an, and name the furniture.

examples.en: Mira is in the canteen.
examples.why: You know this: in + der (dative) for Wo?

examples.en: The sofa is in the living room.
examples.why: New today: furniture, and the same pattern with in, auf and an.

steps: You already know: Wo? + in + the dative (im Büro, in der Kantine, chapter 7); rooms (lesson 1)
New today: furniture words, and auf and an with the same dative: auf dem Tisch, an der Wand
By the end you can: say where eight pieces of furniture are, in a room, on something and at a wall
cards.more: When you move into a flat, you often say where things are: the lamp is on the table, the picture is on the wall, the books are on the shelf. For that you need furniture words and place words. You already know the pattern from chapter 7: a place word, then the dative article. Today it grows from one place word, in, to three: in, auf and an. The pattern and the articles stay the same.

cards.title: Furniture: die Möbel
cards.body: Möbel means furniture, and it is always plural: die Möbel. Learn each piece with its article, because the next cards need it. You know Tisch, Stuhl, Bett, Lampe and Bild already.

examples.en: The sofa is new.
The wardrobe is big.
The furniture is old.

cards.more: Möbel is a funny word. In English furniture is one thing: the furniture is old. In German Möbel is plural: die Möbel sind alt. A single piece has its own name, like Sofa, Sessel or Schrank. Learn each name with der, die or das. The same article will matter in a minute, because the dative article is made from it. For one table you say der Tisch, and later auf dem Tisch.
cards.lead: In the introduction you saw one piece of furniture. This card gives you the whole set of words, with articles and plurals, so you can say where each one is.

deeper.text: Möbel has no singular in everyday German. For one piece, Germans say das Möbelstück, but mostly they just name it: das Sofa, der Schrank. Schrank has a plural with an Umlaut: die Schränke. A Sessel is for one person, a Sofa for two or more. A Regal is open, a Schrank has doors.

example.en: The wardrobes are big.

cards.title: Where is it? Wo? + dative
cards.body: Ask Wo ist ...? and answer with a place word and the dative article: Der Schrank ist im Schlafzimmer. Where something is, the noun after in, auf or an is in the dative.

examples.en: Where is the wardrobe?
The wardrobe is in the bedroom.
examples.why: in dem = im: the dative of das Schlafzimmer.

examples.de: Der Spiegel ist in der Küche.
examples.en: The mirror is in the kitchen.

steps: Ask: Wo ist der Schrank?
Answer: Der Schrank ist + in / auf / an
Add the dative: dem / der / dem / den + n
Der Schrank ist im Schlafzimmer.
cards.more: Wo? means where something is. The answer has three parts: first the thing, then ist, then a small place word with its noun. The noun is in the dative: dem for der-words and das-words, der for die-words. In chapter 7 you used the same words after mit. So you only learn a new place word, and the dative stays the same. Think of the dative as the case of the place where something stays.
cards.lead: Now you know the furniture words. This card shows the question and the answer pattern for the place of a thing, with a place word and the dative that you already know.

deeper.text: For more than one thing, ask Wo sind ...? and answer with sind: Wo sind die Bücher? Die Bücher sind im Regal. The place part does not change, only ist becomes sind. Wo asks only where something is, not where it goes. Where something goes uses a different case, and you learn that in lesson 7.

example.en: Where are the books?

cards.title: in, again: im, in der, in den
cards.body: in means inside. After in, use the dative: in dem = im for der- and das-words, in der for die-words, in den + n for plurals. Die Bücher sind im Regal. Die Teller sind in den Schränken.

examples.en: The books are on the shelf.
examples.why: das Regal → in dem = im Regal.

examples.de: Das Handy ist in der Tasche.
examples.en: The phone is in the bag.

examples.de: Die Teller sind in den Schränken.
examples.en: The plates are in the cupboards.

cards.more: You know in from chapter 7. Now you see all four forms together. For a der-word or das-word, in dem melts into im. For a die-word, you say in der. For plural words, you say in den and add an n to the noun: die Schränke becomes in den Schränken. The extra n is the sign of the dative plural. If the plural already ends in n, you add nothing: in den Küchen.
cards.lead: You answered Wo? with im in lesson 1. This card opens that chunk and shows the whole rule for in: four forms, one for each gender and one for the plural.

deeper.text: The dative plural -n has two exceptions. Plurals that already end in -n stay as they are: in den Küchen. Plurals with -s never take -n: in den Sofas, in den Büros. All other plurals add it: die Zimmer becomes in den Zimmern, die Regale becomes in den Regalen.

example.de: Die Bücher sind in den Regalen.
example.en: The books are on the shelves.

cards.title: auf: on top of
cards.body: auf means on top of a flat surface. Wo is the lamp? Auf dem Tisch. After auf, use the dative: dem for der- and das-words, der for die-words, den + n for plurals.

examples.de: Die Lampe ist auf dem Tisch.
examples.en: The lamp is on the table.

examples.de: Das Buch ist auf dem Sofa.
examples.en: The book is on the sofa.

examples.de: Die Bücher sind auf den Stühlen.
examples.en: The books are on the chairs.

cards.more: Imagine a plate on a table: the plate touches the top of the table. That is auf. Use it for lamps on a table, a cat on a sofa and a book on a carpet. The article after auf is always the dative, because you answer Wo?: auf dem Tisch, auf dem Sofa, auf der Treppe, auf den Stühlen. Auf dem looks like two words, but you cannot melt it into one in the way in dem becomes im. Say auf dem.
cards.lead: In the last card you saw in with the dative. Now you learn auf: the same four dative forms, but a new picture, on top of something.

deeper.text: Write auf dem as two words. In fast speech people sometimes say aufm, but in writing at this level you always use auf dem. The forms for the other genders are the same as with in: auf der, auf den + n.

example.de: Die Katze ist auf dem Teppich.
example.en: The cat is on the carpet.

cards.title: an: at, on the side
cards.body: an means at the side of something or against a vertical surface, like a wall. Das Bild ist an der Wand. an dem becomes am: Der Tisch ist am Fenster. Compare: auf = on top, an = at the side.

examples.de: Das Bild ist an der Wand.
examples.en: The picture is on the wall.
The table is at the window.

examples.de: Der Spiegel ist an der Tür.
examples.en: The mirror is on the door.

steps: auf = on the top: Die Lampe ist auf dem Tisch.
an = at the side: Das Bild ist an der Wand.
an dem = am: Der Tisch ist am Fenster.
an der: an der Tür, an der Wand
cards.more: Picture a wall. A picture hangs at the wall, on the side, not on top. That is an. The same word is used for the table at the window, because the table is next to it. An dem melts into am, just like in dem becomes im. So for a das-word or a der-word you often hear am: am Fenster, am Tisch. For a die-word you say an der: an der Wand, an der Tür.
cards.lead: You know auf for the top. This card adds an for the side or a wall, with the same dative, and it shows how to tell auf and an apart with a mini picture.

deeper.text: In English, on covers both: on the table and on the wall. German splits it in two: auf dem Tisch (on top) and an der Wand (on the side). When you pick a word, imagine the picture: top is auf, side is an.

example.de: Das Foto ist an der Wand.
example.en: The photo is on the wall.

cards.title: The dative table for in, auf, an
cards.body: The three place words use the same dative forms. der-word and das-word: dem (in dem = im, an dem = am). die-word: der. Plural: den + n. Also with ein- and mein-words: einem, einer, meinem, meiner.

examples.de: Das Bild ist an einer Wand.
examples.en: The picture is on a wall.

examples.de: Die Lampe ist auf meinem Tisch.
examples.en: The lamp is on my table.
My phone is in the wardrobe.

cards.more: Now put the three place words in one table. The rule is the same for in, auf and an. For a der-word you need dem. For a das-word you need dem too. For a die-word you need der. For a plural you need den, and an extra n on the noun. If you use ein or mein, the endings follow the same pattern: einem, einer, meinem, meiner. You already know these from chapter 7. So there is only one table to learn, not three.
cards.lead: You have seen in, auf and an one by one. This card puts the three together in one table, so you can see that the dative forms are the same for all of them.

deeper.text: The same table works for every ein-word and possessive: dein, sein, ihr, unser and kein. So you can say Das Handy ist in keinem Zimmer, or Die Lampe ist auf deinem Tisch. Learn dem, der, dem, den once, and every word in the family copies the ending: -em, -er, -em, -en.

example.de: Das Handy ist auf deinem Tisch.
example.en: The phone is on your table.

cards.title: Mix-up: which place word?
cards.body: To choose the place word, imagine the picture: inside is in, on top is auf, at the side is an. Then add the dative article for the noun. All sentences here use ist and answer Wo?

examples.de: Das Handy ist auf dem Teppich.
examples.en: The phone is on the carpet.
The mirror is in the bathroom.

examples.de: Das Foto ist an der Wand.

examples.why: At the side: an der Wand.

rows: Die Lampe ist auf dem Tisch.
Das Bild ist an der Wand.

steps: Inside? in: im Regal
On top? auf: auf dem Tisch
At the side? an: an der Wand
cards.more: You now have three place words and one table. When you want to say where something is, do two small steps. First, look at the picture in your head: is the thing inside, on top, or at the side? That gives you in, auf or an. Second, look at the noun: is it a der-word, a die-word, a das-word or a plural? That gives you dem, der, dem or den. Practice with the sentences on the cards and say them aloud.
cards.lead: You know all three place words and the dative forms. This last card is for practice: two steps, picture first and then the article, so you can answer any Wo? question.

deeper.text: Most of the time, one word fits. A picture is an der Wand, a lamp is auf dem Tisch, a book is im Regal. Sometimes two words fit, and the meaning changes: Der Hund ist auf dem Sofa means on it, but Der Hund ist am Sofa means next to it.

example.en: The lamp is in the living room.

lessons.title: Neben, hinter, vor, zwischen: im Haus
lessons.goal: Say where things and appliances are with neben, hinter, vor, zwischen + dative, and tell long e from short e.

grammar.point: neben (next to), hinter (behind), vor (in front of) and zwischen (between) work exactly like in, auf and an: Wo? needs the dative. zwischen takes two things: zwischen dem Sofa und dem Tisch.
grammar.oneLine: Der Herd ist neben dem Kühlschrank. Der Tisch ist zwischen dem Sofa und der Tür.

mistake.wrong: Der Fernseher ist neben der Sofa.
mistake.right: Der Fernseher ist neben dem Sofa.
mistake.why: Das Sofa is a das-word, so the dative is dem. Only die-words take der. After zwischen, check each noun on its own: zwischen dem Herd und dem Kühlschrank.

terms.meaning: the case you use after the place words when you say where something is
a small word like neben, hinter, vor, zwischen that says where something is
the question word for where something is
the same letter e can be held long (neben) or said short (Teppich)

cards.title: Before we start: next to the fridge
cards.body: In a kitchen you say where things are: the cooker is next to the fridge. You know in, auf and an with the dative from lesson 3, and you know vor from the clock (zehn vor acht). Today four more place words join the group: neben, hinter, vor and zwischen.

examples.de: Das Bild ist an der Wand.
examples.en: The picture is on the wall.
examples.why: You know this: an + der (dative) for Wo?

examples.de: Der Herd ist neben dem Kühlschrank.
examples.en: The cooker is next to the fridge.
examples.why: New today: neben, and the same dative as always.

steps: You already know: in, auf, an + the dative for Wo? (lesson 3), and vor in the clock (zehn vor acht, chapter 5)
New today: neben, hinter, vor, zwischen with the same dative, and the machines of a home
By the end you can: say where the cooker, the washing machine and the TV are, in seven different ways
cards.more: Imagine a toolbox with three tools: in, auf and an. Today four new tools go into the box: neben, hinter, vor and zwischen. The good news: every tool works the same way. You say where something is, then the place word, then the dative article. Nothing about the endings changes. You also meet the machines of a home, like the cooker and the washing machine, and you hear the difference between a long and a short e. You will learn it all step by step in the next cards.

cards.title: Machines in a home: der Herd and friends
cards.body: Kitchens and flats are full of machines. Learn each one with its article, because the next cards need it. You know Kühlschrank, Spülmaschine and Kaffeemaschine already. Six more join them today.

examples.en: The cooker is new.
The washing machine is loud.
The TVs are expensive.
examples.why: Fernseher is plural here, so sind.

cards.more: Every machine has its own article, and you simply learn it together with the word. Look at the endings: words that end in -e, like Waschmaschine and Mikrowelle, are usually die-words. Words that end in -er, like Fernseher and Staubsauger, are usually der-words. Those -er words do not change in the plural. You say der Fernseher and die Fernseher. Learn the table below and use it as your small dictionary for the next cards.
cards.lead: In the introduction you saw the cooker next to the fridge. On this card you meet the machines of a flat with their articles, so that you can say where each one is.

deeper.text: Words that end in -er and name a machine or a tool are usually der-words, and the plural looks the same: der Staubsauger, die Staubsauger. A good habit: when you see a new -er word for a thing, guess der. You will often be right.

example.de: Der Staubsauger ist alt und laut.
example.en: The vacuum cleaner is old and loud.

cards.title: neben: next to
cards.body: neben means next to, side by side. Where something is, the noun after neben is in the dative, like after in, auf and an: neben dem Herd, neben der Tür, neben dem Bett, neben den Stühlen.

examples.de: Der Kühlschrank ist neben dem Herd.
examples.en: The fridge is next to the cooker.

examples.de: Der Fernseher ist neben der Tür.
examples.en: The TV is next to the door.

examples.de: Die Lampen sind neben den Betten.
examples.en: The lamps are next to the beds.
examples.why: plural: den + n. Betten already ends in n, so nothing is added.

cards.more: Picture two chairs in a row. One chair is neben the other: they stand side by side. After neben you answer Wo?, so the dative comes. You know the four forms: dem for der-words and das-words, der for die-words, den for the plural, plus an n on the noun. Betten already ends in n, so it stays Betten. Neben never melts together with dem, so you say neben dem, in two words.
cards.lead: You can now name the machines. On this card the first new place word: neben. You will see that it takes the same dative forms as in, auf and an, so you only learn one new word.

deeper.text: neben only says the two things are side by side. It does not say which side. For that, put links (left) or rechts (right) in front: links neben dem Sofa, rechts neben dem Herd. In a flat viewing you hear this all the time, because it helps you picture the room without seeing it.

example.de: Der Fernseher ist links neben dem Sofa.
example.en: The TV is on the left, next to the sofa.

cards.title: hinter and vor: behind, in front of
cards.body: hinter means behind; vor means in front of. Both answer Wo? with the dative: hinter dem Sofa, vor dem Haus. You know vor from the clock too, and it also means before in time. One word, three jobs.

examples.de: Die Katze ist hinter dem Sofa.
examples.en: The cat is behind the sofa.

examples.de: Der Hund ist vor der Tür.
examples.en: The dog is in front of the door.

examples.de: Wir trinken vor dem Essen Tee.
examples.en: We drink tea before the meal.
examples.why: vor in time = before. Also with the dative.

steps: vor + place = in front of: vor dem Haus
vor + time = before: vor dem Essen
vor + clock = to: zehn vor acht
In all three: the noun after vor is in the dative
cards.more: Hinter and vor are opposites. If you stand in front of a door, you are vor der Tür. If you hide behind the door, you are hinter der Tür. The word vor has two more jobs. In time it means before: vor dem Essen is before the meal. On the clock it means to: zehn vor acht is ten to eight. In all three jobs, the next noun is in the dative, so the pattern stays easy.
cards.lead: Now that you know neben, this card adds two opposites, hinter and vor. You will also see that vor does three jobs: place, time and clock. That helps you read it in every sentence.

deeper.text: The opposite of vor in time is nach: vor dem Essen, nach dem Essen. Both take the dative, just like vor as a place. You know nach from the clock too: zehn nach acht. So with two small words you can order a whole day: vor dem Frühstück, nach dem Frühstück, nach der Arbeit.

example.de: Nach dem Essen trinken wir Kaffee.
example.en: After the meal we drink coffee.

cards.title: zwischen: between two things
cards.body: zwischen means between, and it needs two things joined by und. Each noun gets its own dative article: zwischen dem Herd und dem Kühlschrank. Check each article, do not copy the first one.

examples.de: Der Tisch ist zwischen dem Sofa und dem Fenster.
examples.en: The table is between the sofa and the window.
examples.why: das Sofa → dem, das Fenster → dem.

examples.de: Das Bett ist zwischen der Tür und dem Schrank.
examples.en: The bed is between the door and the wardrobe.
examples.why: die Tür → der, der Schrank → dem.

examples.de: Die Waschmaschine ist zwischen der Dusche und der Tür.
examples.en: The washing machine is between the shower and the door.
examples.why: die Dusche → der, die Tür → der.

rows: zwischen dem Herd und dem Kühlschrank
zwischen der Tür und dem Fenster
zwischen den Betten und der Lampe

cards.more: Between means in the middle of two things, so German needs two things: zwischen A und B. Both nouns follow the same rule as everything else: look at each noun and choose its dative article. Der Herd gives dem Herd. Die Tür gives der Tür. Do not use the same article twice just because it sounds right. Say each noun with its own article.
cards.lead: You know three more place words now. This card adds the last one of today, zwischen. It is a little different, because it needs two nouns and the word und.

deeper.text: zwischen can also be used with a plural: zwischen den Stühlen means between the chairs. Then you need no und, because the plural already gives you more than one thing. The article is den, and the noun gets an n if needed.

example.de: Das Handy ist zwischen den Stühlen.
example.en: The phone is between the chairs.

cards.title: All seven in one table
cards.body: You now know seven place words: in, auf, an, neben, hinter, vor, zwischen. All of them answer Wo? with the dative, and the endings never change. Same rule, new words. Two more words come in the next lesson.

examples.de: Das Buch ist auf dem Tisch.
examples.en: The book is on the table.

examples.de: Die Lampe ist neben dem Bett.
examples.en: The lamp is next to the bed.

examples.de: Das Handy ist hinter der Lampe.
examples.en: The phone is behind the lamp.

rows: zwischen dem Herd und der Tür

cards.more: Think of the seven words as seven doors into the same room. Each door has a different name, but behind every door waits the same dative: dem, der, dem, den + n. That is why you do not need seven rules. You need one rule and seven words. Look at the table and say each place word with dem Tisch out loud. Then switch to der Tür. The pattern will feel automatic very soon.
cards.lead: You have seen the new place words one by one. Now this card puts all seven side by side, so you can see that the rule stays the same for every word.

deeper.text: A memory trick: learn the place word and its article as one chunk, such as neben dem, hinter der, vor dem. Your brain stores the chunk, and you do not have to think about the case again while you speak.

example.en: Mira is behind the door.

cards.title: Wo ist ...? Ask, answer and add mein
cards.body: Ask Wo ist ...? and answer with ist and a place chunk. With mein you add the dative ending: neben meinem Bett (der, das), neben meiner Lampe (die), neben meinen Büchern (plural, + n).

examples.en: Where is your phone?

examples.de: Mein Handy ist neben meinem Bett.
examples.en: My phone is next to my bed.

examples.de: Meine Bücher sind hinter meiner Lampe.
examples.en: My books are behind my lamp.

cards.more: A good question has a good answer. Ask Wo ist dein Handy? and answer in a whole sentence: Mein Handy ist neben meinem Bett. The word mein follows the same dative pattern you know from ein: meinem for der- and das-words, meiner for die-words, meinen for plurals. Your place chunk always sits at the end of the sentence, and ist stays in second place.
cards.lead: You can build a place chunk with the, now you add my. This card shows the full question and answer, and the dative of mein, so you can talk about your own things.

deeper.text: In real talk you often answer with only the place chunk, without a full sentence. Wo ist der Kühlschrank? Neben dem Herd. That is natural and polite. At this level both ways are fine, so use the full sentence when you write.

example.en: Next to the cooker.

cards.title: Say it right: long e and short e
cards.body: The letter e can sound long or short. Often it is long before one consonant (neben, Regal) and short before two consonants (Fernseher, Mikrowelle, Teppich). Listen for the length, it changes the sound.

examples.de: Das Regal ist neben dem Herd.
examples.en: The shelf is next to the cooker.

examples.de: Der Teppich ist hinter dem Sofa.
examples.en: The carpet is behind the sofa.

examples.de: Der Sessel ist vor dem Fernseher.
examples.en: The armchair is in front of the TV.
examples.why: Ses-sel and Fern-se-her: short e at the start.

rows: one consonant after it, or ee
two consonants after it, or a double letter
long e, although two consonants follow

cards.more: A long e sounds like the e in the English word they, but pure and held longer. A short e sounds like the e in bed. How do you know which one? Look at what comes after the e. One consonant: usually long. Two consonants, or a double letter like pp or ss: short. It is only a rule of thumb, and some words are exceptions, like Herd, which has a long e. Say the words aloud and listen.
cards.lead: You have all seven place words. This last card is about sound: long e and short e. It helps you say words like neben, Regal and Teppich so that people understand you.

deeper.text: An e at the very end of a word, or in an ending like -en, is neither long nor short: it is a soft, quick sound like the a in English sofa. Listen to Kiste, Lampe, Ecke, stehen. Do not say it like a clear e. This soft e is one of the most common sounds in German.

example.de: Die Lampe steht in der Ecke.
example.en: The lamp stands in the corner.

lessons.title: Über, unter und die Verben stehen, liegen, hängen, sitzen
lessons.goal: Complete all nine place words (über, unter) and say how things are: standing, lying, hanging, sitting.

grammar.point: über (above) and unter (under) take the dative for Wo?. The verbs stehen (upright), liegen (flat), hängen (on a wall or from above) and sitzen (people and animals) all answer Wo? and take the dative.
grammar.oneLine: Das Bild hängt an der Wand. Die Katze sitzt auf dem Sofa.

mistake.wrong: Das Bild hängt auf die Wand.
mistake.right: Das Bild hängt an der Wand.
mistake.why: A picture hangs at the side of a wall, so you say an. Wo? (where it is) needs the dative: die Wand becomes der Wand.

terms.meaning: the case you use after the nine place words when you say where something is
a verb like stehen, liegen, hängen, sitzen that says how something is placed
the question word for where something is
the verb without -en: steh-, lieg-, häng-, sitz-

cards.title: Before we start: the picture hangs on the wall
cards.body: You tell a friend about your room: the lamp stands in the corner, the book lies on the bed, the picture hangs on the wall. Until now you said ist for everything. Today two last place words join the group, and four verbs say how a thing is.

examples.de: Das Bild ist an der Wand.
examples.en: The picture is on the wall.
examples.why: You know this: ist + an + the dative (Wo?).

examples.de: Das Bild hängt an der Wand.
examples.en: The picture hangs on the wall.
examples.why: New today: hängt says more than ist. The dative stays.

steps: You already know: Wo ist ...? + the dative with seven place words (lessons 3 and 4), and regular verb endings -e, -st, -t (chapter 1)
New today: über and unter, and the verbs stehen, liegen, hängen, sitzen: they also take the dative
By the end you can: say where a thing is and how it is there: standing, lying, hanging or sitting
cards.more: Think of a photo of a room. With ist you say that the lamp is somewhere. With stehen, liegen, hängen and sitzen you say how it is there: standing up, lying flat, hanging or sitting. English often just says is, but German is more exact. It feels like adding colour to a black and white drawing. The place words and the dative stay the same. You only swap one small verb. We take it step by step: first two new place words, then the four verbs.

cards.title: über and unter: above and under
cards.body: über means above, unter means under. Both answer Wo? with the dative: über dem Tisch, unter dem Bett, unter der Lampe. Über does not touch the thing. Auf does touch it.

examples.de: Die Lampe ist über dem Tisch.
examples.en: The lamp is above the table.

examples.de: Der Hund ist unter dem Bett.
examples.en: The dog is under the bed.

examples.de: Die Katze ist unter der Treppe.
examples.en: The cat is under the stairs.

steps: über: above, up (über dem Tisch)
the thing in the middle: der Tisch
unter: below, down (unter dem Tisch)
cards.more: Draw a table on a piece of paper. Put an arrow pointing up above it: that is über. Put an arrow pointing down below it: that is unter. The table in the middle gets the dative, because you answer Wo?. So you say über dem Tisch and unter dem Tisch. If the lamp is on the table, you say auf dem Tisch, because it touches the table. If it is above it, in the air, you say über.
cards.lead: You know seven place words. On this card two more arrive, über and unter. They are opposites, and they use the same dative as the others.

deeper.text: When you do not name the thing below, use oben (up, upstairs) and unten (down, downstairs) on their own: Die Lampe ist oben. Das Bad ist unten. They need no article and no case. über and unter always need a noun after them: über dem Tisch. So oben is the short form when the place is clear.

example.en: The bathroom is downstairs.

cards.title: stehen: standing upright
cards.body: stehen says that something stands upright: Der Schrank steht in der Ecke. It answers Wo? and takes the dative. The endings are regular: ich stehe, du stehst, er steht, wir stehen, ihr steht, sie stehen.

examples.de: Der Schrank steht in der Ecke.
examples.en: The wardrobe stands in the corner.
examples.why: die Ecke = the corner; in der Ecke.

examples.de: Die Lampe steht neben dem Sofa.
examples.en: The lamp stands next to the sofa.

examples.de: Die Flaschen stehen auf dem Tisch.
examples.en: The bottles stand on the table.

rows: Der Schrank steht in der Ecke.
Die Flaschen stehen auf dem Tisch.

cards.more: Stehen is a regular verb. Take off -en and you get the stem steh-. Then add the ending: -e for ich, -st for du, -t for er, sie and es, -en for wir and sie, -t for ihr. You know this pattern from chapter 1. Use stehen for things that have a base and stand up: a wardrobe, a lamp, a bottle, a chair. It also answers Wo?, so the place chunk after it is dative.
cards.lead: You now have all nine place words. This card adds the first position verb, stehen, for things that stand upright, and shows that its endings are the ones you already know.

deeper.text: In German, people and buildings stand too: Mira steht hinter der Tür, and Das Haus steht im Park. English says is in many of these cases, but German likes to say stehen when something is upright. So stehen is much more common than you might think.

example.en: The house stands in the park.

cards.title: liegen: lying flat
cards.body: liegen says that something lies flat: Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch. Use stehen for upright things and liegen for flat ones. Forms: ich liege, du liegst, er liegt, wir liegen, ihr liegt, sie liegen.

examples.de: Das Buch liegt auf dem Bett.
examples.en: The book lies on the bed.

examples.de: Das Handy liegt neben der Lampe.
examples.en: The phone lies next to the lamp.

examples.de: Der Teppich liegt auf dem Boden.
examples.en: The carpet lies on the floor.
examples.why: der Boden = the floor (plural: die Böden).

rows: Der Schrank steht in der Ecke.
Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
Die Lampe steht neben dem Sofa.
Das Handy liegt neben der Lampe.
Die Flasche steht auf dem Tisch.
Der Teppich liegt auf dem Boden.

cards.more: Think of how the thing looks. A bottle stands up, so it steht. A book on a table is flat, so it liegt. A carpet on the floor, a phone on a bed, a pen on a desk: all liegen. The ending pattern is the same as for stehen: ich liege, du liegst, er liegt. The place chunk after liegen is dative, because you answer Wo?. The verb is in second place as always.
cards.lead: Now you know stehen. This card adds its partner, liegen, for flat things, and puts both in a small table so you can see the difference at once.

deeper.text: The same thing can use two verbs, depending on its position. A book stands upright on a shelf and lies flat on a table. So the question is not what the thing is, but how it is placed. Look at the picture in your head.

example.en: The book stands on the shelf.

cards.title: hängen and sitzen: on the wall, sitting
cards.body: hängen says that something hangs on a wall or from above: Das Bild hängt an der Wand. sitzen is for people and animals: Die Katze sitzt auf dem Sofa. Both answer Wo? and take the dative.

examples.de: Das Bild hängt an der Wand.
examples.en: The picture hangs on the wall.

examples.de: Die Lampe hängt an der Decke.
examples.en: The lamp hangs from the ceiling.

examples.de: Die Katze sitzt auf dem Sofa.
examples.en: The cat sits on the sofa.

cards.more: Two more verbs complete the set. Hängen is for things that hang, such as a picture on a wall or a lamp from the ceiling. Sitzen is for living things, for example a cat on a sofa or Anna at the window. Both use the same endings as stehen, with one small change: du sitzt, not sitzst. The place chunk after both verbs is dative, so a wall is an der Wand.
cards.lead: You have stehen and liegen. This card adds the last two position verbs: hängen for things on the wall or the ceiling, and sitzen for people and animals.

deeper.text: With sitzen the stem ends in z, so du sitzt, not du sitzst. The s of the ending melts into the z. It is the same with heißen in chapter 1: du heißt. So you never write zst or ßst: you write just -t.

example.en: You sit next to the window.

cards.title: Choosing the verb
cards.body: Ask yourself how the thing is. Upright? stehen. Flat? liegen. On a wall or hanging from above? hängen. A person or animal sitting? sitzen. If you are not sure, ist is always correct.

examples.de: Das Handy liegt neben dem Bett.
examples.en: The phone lies next to the bed.

examples.de: Die Heizung hängt unter dem Fenster.
examples.en: The radiator hangs under the window.
examples.why: die Heizung = the radiator; on the wall: hängt.

examples.en: Mira sits on the chair.

rows: Der Schrank steht in der Ecke.
Das Buch liegt auf dem Bett.
Das Bild hängt an der Wand.
Die Katze sitzt unter dem Tisch.

steps: Upright, with a base? → stehen (der Schrank steht)
Flat? → liegen (das Buch liegt)
On a wall or hanging from above? → hängen (das Bild hängt)
A person or animal sitting? → sitzen (die Katze sitzt)
Not sure? → ist
cards.more: A good way to choose is a short quiz in your head. Is it a person or an animal who sits? Then sitzen. Is the thing fixed to a wall or ceiling? Then hängen. Is it flat? Then liegen. Does it stand on a base, upright? Then stehen. If you cannot decide, say ist: Das Glas ist auf dem Tisch is correct too. Over time, you will pick the right verb without asking yourself.
cards.lead: You know all four verbs. This card gives you a small decision tree, so that you can pick the right verb quickly when you describe a room.

deeper.text: liegen is not only for books. Germans also use it for towns and places on a map: Hamburg liegt im Norden, Die Wohnung liegt im Zentrum. In flat ads you read this all the time. So liegen can mean is located. For people lying in bed it is the normal word too: Leon liegt im Bett.

example.en: The flat is in the centre.

cards.title: All nine at a glance
cards.body: You now know all nine place words: an, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, zwischen. They are in alphabetical order here, which helps you remember them. With Wo? they always take the dative.

examples.de: Der Hund sitzt zwischen dem Sessel und dem Sofa.
examples.en: The dog sits between the armchair and the sofa.

examples.de: Das Bild hängt über dem Bett.
examples.en: The picture hangs above the bed.

examples.de: Die Katze sitzt unter dem Tisch.
examples.en: The cat sits under the table.

rows: zwischen dem Herd und der Tür

cards.more: Nine place words sound like a lot, but you really have one rule: for Wo?, use the dative. The alphabet gives you an easy memory aid. Say them in order: an, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, zwischen. Say it three times a day for a week, and the list will stay in your head. These nine words are special: in lesson 7 you will see that the same words can also answer Wohin?.
cards.lead: You have collected all the place words, one by one. This card lines up all nine in one table, so you see the whole group and its one rule.

deeper.text: These nine words are called two-way words (Wechselpräpositionen), because in lesson 7 they also answer a second question, Wohin?, with another case. Other place words, like bei and mit from chapter 7, always take the dative and never change. For today, remember only this: Wo? with these nine always means the dative.

example.de: Der Stuhl steht vor der Heizung.
example.en: The chair stands in front of the radiator.

cards.title: Place first: Im Wohnzimmer steht ein Sofa
cards.body: You can start a sentence with the place: Im Wohnzimmer steht ein Sofa. The verb stays in second place, and the subject moves behind it. You know this from time words: Heute arbeite ich.

examples.en: In the living room there is a sofa.
examples.why: Place first, then the verb, then the subject.

rows: Ein Bild hängt an der Wand.

steps: Place chunk first: Im Wohnzimmer
Verb second: steht
Subject after the verb: ein Sofa
cards.more: In German the verb always takes the second place. The first place can be the subject, a time word, or the place. If you start with Im Wohnzimmer, the verb comes next: steht. The subject, ein Sofa, now comes after the verb. It is like a stage: first you set the scene, then you say what is there. This is how people describe a room in stories and in flat ads.
cards.lead: You know all nine place words and four verbs. The last card shows how to start a sentence with the place, so that you describe a room like a story.

deeper.text: This order is natural when you describe a room. First you say where, then what is there. The new thing comes last in the sentence. So the listener first sees the empty place in their mind, then you put something into it.

lessons.title: Wer wohnt wo? Allein, mit, bei
lessons.goal: Say what kind of home you live in and who you live with.

grammar.point: wohnen answers Wo?, so in takes the dative: in einem Hochhaus, in einer WG. mit and bei always take the dative: mit meinem Bruder, bei meinen Eltern. auf dem Land is a fixed chunk, and allein never changes.
grammar.oneLine: Ich wohne in einer WG. Ich wohne mit meiner Schwester.

mistake.why: After mit you need the dative: der Bruder becomes meinem Bruder.

terms.meaning: the case you use after in, mit and bei when you say where or with whom you live
a flat shared by several people (short for Wohngemeinschaft)
a person you share a home with
a phrase you learn as one piece, like auf dem Land

cards.title: Before we start: who lives with you?
cards.body: Where do you live, and with whom? These are the first questions new neighbours ask. You can already say Ich wohne in Berlin, and you know mit with the dative from chapter 7. Today you describe your kind of home and the people in it.

examples.en: I live in Berlin.
examples.why: You know this: wohnen + in + a city.

examples.en: I live in a shared flat.
examples.why: New today: in + the dative with a kind of home.

steps: You already know: Ich wohne in Berlin (chapter 1) and mit + the dative: mit meinem Freund (chapter 7)
New today: kinds of homes (WG, Hochhaus ...) and wohnen in / mit / bei + the dative
By the end you can: say what kind of home you live in and who lives there with you
cards.more: Imagine you are at a party and a new person asks: Wo wohnst du? Mit wem? Those two questions open a conversation. You have most of the pieces already: wohnen, in, mit and the dative from chapter 7. Today you add the names of different homes, like WG and Hochhaus, and the little word bei, which means at someone's place. You will practise it step by step, one small card at a time, so it feels like a real chat.

cards.title: Kinds of homes: WG, Hochhaus and more
cards.body: People live in different kinds of homes. A WG is a flat that several people share. A Hochhaus is a tower block, a Reihenhaus is a house in a row, a Studentenwohnheim is a student hall. Learn each with its article.

examples.de: Mein Bruder wohnt in einer WG.
examples.en: My brother lives in a shared flat.
Anna lives in a tower block.

examples.de: Herr Ali wohnt in einem Reihenhaus.
examples.en: Herr Ali lives in a terraced house.

cards.more: A WG is short for Wohngemeinschaft, which means a living community: three or four people share one flat and each has their own room. A Hochhaus is a high house, a tall building with many flats. A Reihenhaus is a row house: many houses stand next to each other in a row. A Studentenwohnheim is a house for students. Learn each word with its article, because you will say in einem or in einer before it.
cards.lead: In the introduction you said Ich wohne in einer WG. On this card you meet the kinds of homes, with their articles and plurals, so you can say what you live in.

deeper.text: People say WG letter by letter: weh-geh. It is an abbreviation, and nobody says the long word in daily talk. The plural is die WGs, with an s, like many short words and abbreviations. So remember: one WG, two WGs.

example.de: Meine Freunde wohnen in einer WG.
example.en: My friends live in a shared flat.

cards.title: Wo wohnst du? in + dative with ein
cards.body: Ask Wo wohnst du? and answer with in and the dative: in einem Hochhaus (der- and das-words), in einer WG (die-words). With mein: in meinem Haus, in meiner Wohnung. Wohnen answers Wo?, so it uses the dative.

examples.en: Where do you live?
I live in a tower block.

examples.de: Mira wohnt in einer Wohnung im Zentrum.
examples.en: Mira lives in a flat in the centre.
examples.why: die Wohnung → einer; im Zentrum = in dem Zentrum.

steps: Ask: Wo wohnst du?
Answer: Ich wohne + in
Add the dative: einem / einer / einem
Ich wohne in einem Hochhaus.
cards.more: Wohnen tells you where you stay, not where you go. That means it answers Wo?, and so the noun after in is in the dative. You already know the dative of ein from chapter 7: einem for der- and das-words, einer for die-words. With mein it is the same: in meinem Haus, in meiner Wohnung. So you only need to say whether the home is a der-, die- or das-word.
cards.lead: You know the names of the homes. Now you learn the question Wo wohnst du? and the answer with in + the dative, so you can say exactly where you live.

deeper.text: If you give a city or a country, you use no article and no dative ending: Ich wohne in Berlin. You only need the dative with in when there is an article, like in einer Wohnung. So Ich wohne in einer Wohnung in Berlin has both.

example.de: Wir wohnen in einem Haus in Köln.
example.en: We live in a house in Cologne.

cards.title: Mit wem? mit, bei and allein
cards.body: Mit wem wohnst du? Use mit and the dative: mit meinem Bruder, mit meiner Schwester, mit meinen Eltern. bei means at someone's place: bei meinen Eltern. allein means alone and never changes.

examples.en: I live with my brother.

examples.de: Mein Freund wohnt bei seinen Eltern.
examples.en: My friend lives with his parents.
examples.why: plural: seinen Eltern, and Eltern already ends in n.

examples.en: Ben lives alone.

cards.more: Two small words answer Mit wem?. Mit means with: you share the home, for example mit meiner Schwester. Bei means at the place of someone: bei meinen Eltern means in my parents' home. After both words you need the dative. The possessive word follows the same pattern as ein: meinem, meiner, meinen + n. Allein is an adverb: it never gets an ending.
cards.lead: You said where you live. Now comes the second question, with whom. This card adds mit, bei and allein, so you can name the people at home.

deeper.text: Natives often add zusammen (together): Ich wohne mit meinem Bruder zusammen. And mit and bei are not the same. Ich wohne mit meinen Eltern means we share a home. Ich wohne bei meinen Eltern means I live in their home: it is their flat, not mine. Many young people wohnen bei den Eltern.

example.de: Ich wohne mit meinem Bruder zusammen.
example.en: I live together with my brother.

cards.title: In der Stadt, auf dem Land
cards.body: Two chunks say where your home is: in der Stadt (in the city) and auf dem Land (in the countryside). Say auf dem Land, not in dem Land: it is a fixed chunk. Learn it as one piece.

examples.en: Mira lives in the city.

examples.de: Meine Eltern wohnen auf dem Land.
examples.en: My parents live in the countryside.
We live in the centre.

cards.more: Some chunks you simply learn as pieces. In German you live in der Stadt, but auf dem Land. Why auf? Think of the land as a wide flat field, and you live on top of it. In English we also say in the city, but in the country. Learn auf dem Land as one block and you cannot go wrong. The word das Land also means country. The plural is die Länder.
cards.lead: You can say what home you live in and with whom. This card adds two chunks that say where the home is: in the city or in the countryside.

deeper.text: The word Land has two meanings: the countryside, and a country like Deutschland. The plural is die Länder, with an Umlaut. The context tells you which meaning is meant: auf dem Land is the countryside, and Deutschland ist ein Land is a country.

example.en: Germany is a country.

cards.title: Mitbewohner, Haustier and teilen
cards.body: A Mitbewohner is a person you share a home with (Mitbewohnerin for a woman). A Haustier is a pet. You share things: Wir teilen die Küche. Forms of teilen: ich teile, du teilst, er teilt.

cards.more: In a flat share you live with your Mitbewohner. The word is made from mit and Bewohner, which means with and resident. A Haustier is an animal in the house, such as a cat or a dog. You teilen, which means you share, things like the kitchen, the bathroom or the washing machine. The verb is regular: the stem teil- takes the normal endings you know from chapter 1.
cards.lead: You know where you live and with whom. This card gives you three words that belong to shared life: Mitbewohner, Haustier and the verb teilen.

deeper.text: To say a woman, add -in: der Mitbewohner, die Mitbewohnerin. It is the same pattern as Freund and Freundin. The plural of the woman's word is die Mitbewohnerinnen, with a double n. When a group has men and women, the plural die Mitbewohner is used.

example.en: She is my flatmate.

cards.title: Culture: life in a WG
cards.body: Many young people in Germany live in a WG or a Studentenwohnheim. They share the kitchen and often the bathroom. A Putzplan is a cleaning plan: it says who cleans what. Mitbewohner are flatmates, not family.

examples.en: We have a cleaning plan.

examples.de: In der WG teilen wir die Küche.
examples.en: In the shared flat we share the kitchen.
examples.why: place first: the verb stays second.

examples.en: The student hall is not expensive.

cards.more: In a WG each person has their own room, and everyone shares the kitchen and often the bathroom. To keep it fair, many flats have a Putzplan. Mitbewohner are not family, and they do not have to be friends. They often meet in the kitchen, cook together and talk. In a Studentenwohnheim the rooms are mostly small, and the kitchen can be shared by a whole floor.
cards.lead: This is the last card of the lesson. You learned the homes, the people and the words for shared life. Now a little culture, and then moving day waits in the next lesson.

deeper.text: The kitchen is the heart of a WG. People often meet there in the evening to eat and talk. Rent is usually shared, so a room in a WG costs less than a whole flat. That is one reason why so many students choose a WG.

example.de: Die Küche ist in einer WG sehr wichtig.
example.en: The kitchen is very important in a shared flat.

lessons.title: Umzug: Wohin damit? in, auf, an + Akkusativ
lessons.goal: Say where you put things (wohin?) with stellen, legen, hängen + accusative, and keep Wo? (dative) and Wohin? (accusative) apart.

grammar.point: After an, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, zwischen: Wo? (it is there) takes the dative, Wohin? (you put it there) takes the accusative. Pairs: stehen/stellen, liegen/legen, hängen/hängen. in das = ins, an das = ans, auf das = aufs.

mistake.right: Ich stelle die Lampe auf den Tisch.
mistake.why: You are putting the lamp there (wohin?), so you need the accusative: den. Dem is only for Wo? (it is already there).

terms.meaning: Wo? (no movement) = dative; Wohin? (movement) = accusative
der becomes den; die, das and plural die stay
